message.content:
Eigenvalues \(k\) are the values for which
\[
\det(A-kI)=0.
\]
Here
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-2&1\\2&-3&2\\-1&2&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Compute:
\[
A-kI=
\begin{pmatrix}
2-k&-2&1\\
2&-3-k&2\\
-1&2&-k
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
\det(A-kI)
=(2-k)((-3-k)(-k)-4)+2(2(-k)-2(-1))+(2\cdot2-(-3-k)(-1)).
\]
Simplifying,
\[
\det(A-kI)=-k^3-k^2+5k-3.
\]
So
\[
-k^3-k^2+5k-3=0
\]
or
\[
k^3+k^2-5k+3=0.
\]
Factor:
\[
k^3+k^2-5k+3=(k-1)^2(k+3).
\]
Thus the eigenvalues are
\[
k=1 \quad \text{and} \quad k=-3.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\{-3,1\}}\).
